title: C02/D02: independent runtime parity for a dynamic population-map rate
reason: NFnext synthesized executable map rules; independent pure-death check executed 2026-11-19
scope: Simple particle-pattern maps with a declared componentless population product and a constant or Molecules-observable arithmetic rate. Other shapes remain fail-closed.

recorded_evidence.local_revision: working tree at b5e1ea60 plus the NFnext dynamic-rate changes in this tree (not a hosted exact-main receipt)
recorded_evidence.independent_oracle: Gillespie SSA with its own RNG for lambda(n)=k*n^2; also cross-checked against a forward-Kolmogorov ODE solution
recorded_evidence.measured: NFnext U(T=1) mean 49.9043 (se 0.1603) vs independent SSA mean 49.8633; frozen-rate wrong law 36.7879
recorded_evidence.classification: analytic parity AND pinned-native NFsim law parity passed locally for the supported population-map shape; dynamic energy remains analytic-only by documented oracle disposition (see native_parity_attempt)

native_parity_attempt.oracle: RuleWorld/NFsim 8c449bbccc4a0c54586ae562f46f4955e65fe876, locally built; SHA-256 caf0ad15f23169d13ff9634a5075337e915a0931a823522d3b0c5ca10253800a matches provenance/upstreams.lock.yml
native_parity_attempt.dynamic_energy: BNG3 XML with ep1: A(x~u) G0 * NB() is rejected by native NFsim: 'cannot evaluate energy expression (G0 * NB()) ... Undefined token NB'. Canonical tools do not implement observable-dependent energy, so per DECISIONS item 16 only the analytic law is a valid oracle.
native_parity_attempt.population_map: A valid independent encoding was established: an equivalent native NFsim law (A(x~u) -> 0 with global rate function k*U) generated from independently written BNGL by pinned BNG2 9601746f8884ed19ab2acea49fe87fc4660ace46 and run by pinned native NFsim. Native NFsim binds observables as muParser variables (Observable::addReferenceToMyself -> DefineVar(obsName, &count)), so BNGL's U() spelling is rewritten to U as a documented spelling translation, not a law change. BNG2's own hybrid HPP was NOT used as the oracle because it pre-lumps initial particles into the population and does not exercise NFnext's direct conversion dynamics.
native_parity_attempt.population_map_result: 512 fixed seeds: NFnext mean U(T=1)=49.9043, pinned native NFsim mean=50.1152, difference 0.2109 within 4-sigma band 0.9418, two-sample KS=0.055 (95% threshold ~0.101). Reproduce with tests/validation/release/cases/issue-147/test_nfnext_dynamic_map_native_parity.py (NFSIM_BIN and BNG2_PERL required; absent oracles are NOT_TESTED).
native_parity_attempt.energy_disposition: Native NFsim's energy parser (NFinput/NFinput_energy.cpp:33-49, evaluateEnergyExpression) binds only parameters, never observables. The observable-dependent energy expression is therefore outside the pinned native oracle by construction; it cannot be re-encoded without changing the semantic family. Per DECISIONS item 16 the independent analytic detailed-balance law is the valid oracle for that extension, and native parity stays explicitly NOT_TESTED.
native_parity_attempt.consequence: The dynamic population-map law has independent analytic AND pinned-native evidence locally. Dynamic energy remains analytic-only by documented oracle disposition. Full corpus acceptance and default promotion still require the hosted exact-main gate.

purpose: Record the check identity, independent oracles, seed budget and error control for the supported dynamic population-map runtime shape, together with locally executed analytic and pinned-native results. Full corpus acceptance and default promotion remain separate release clauses.

subject_model.source:
begin parameters
  k_gather 0.01
end parameters
begin molecule types
  A(x~u)
end molecule types
begin population types
  A_pop()
end population types
begin seed species
  A(x~u) 100
end seed species
begin observables
  Molecules U A(x~u)
end observables
begin reaction rules
  A(x~u) -> A(x~u) k_gather
end reaction rules
begin population maps
  A(x~u) -> A_pop() k_gather * U()
end population maps
end model
subject_model.source_semantics: The pinned BNG2 lowers the dynamic population-map rate into an observable-dependent rate law on the generated map rule: _rateLaw1() = k_gather*U() attached to _MapRule0: A(x~u) -> A_pop() _rateLaw1(). Each conversion removes one A particle that U counts; U therefore decreases by one per event. No expected value or tolerance is normalised to BNG3 output.

analytic_law.rate_law: a(U) = k * U() * (# reactant embeddings) = k * U * U = k * U^2
analytic_law.ctmc: Pure-death: U -> U-1 at total rate a(U) = k*U^2 (equivalently U -> U+1 with the analogous rate for the growth/conversion convention), absorbing at U=0. The observable is re-evaluated after every event, so the propensity is state-dependent, not frozen.
analytic_law.mean_field_caveat: dU/dt = -k*U^2 is only a large-count approximation; the oracle is the exact CTMC, not the mean-field law. U0/(1+k*U0*t) is not an independent oracle.
analytic_law.independent_oracle: Exact Gillespie SSA written independently of BNG3 (own RNG): draw tau ~ Exp(k*u*u), decrement u by one, repeat until the sample time. This is the same oracle pattern qualified for observable-dependent rates in tests/python/nfnext/test_nfnext_dynamic_rate_observable.py.
analytic_law.checked_quantity: Ensemble mean and distribution of U(T) for the declared sample grid, starting from U0=100.

wrong_law.law: a_wrong(U) = k * U0 * U (observable sampled once at its initial value and never invalidated), producing exponential decay U0*exp(-k*U0*t) instead of the state-dependent pure-death distribution.
wrong_law.requirement: The comparator must accept the state-dependent CTMC law and reject this frozen-rate law by more than the stated error control.

seed_policy.seeds: seed_base .. seed_base + n_runs - 1; identical fixed set for the NFnext route and the independent SSA oracle
seed_policy.budget_note: At least 200 runs, fixed and recorded; no retry or exclusion adjusts the budget after observing results.

dkw.epsilon: sqrt(ln(2/alpha)/(2*n_runs)) applied to the empirical CDF of the count observable against the exact CTMC law

error_control.standard_error: 4 empirical standard errors on the difference of NFnext and independent-SSA ensemble means
error_control.distributional: two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov plus two-sample Hoeffding bound on the ensemble sums when the native NFsim oracle is available
error_control.classification: passed / unsupported / failed / timed out / invalid source are reported separately; an absent oracle is NOT_TESTED, never a pass

nfsim.build_recipe: cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DNFSIM_BUILD_EXECUTABLE=ON -DNFSIM_BUILD_LIBRARY=OFF; cmake --build build --target NFsim --parallel 1 (AppleClang 21.0.0.21000334, macOS arm64).

acceptance_when_enabled: NFnext executes the lowered dynamic population-map rate with the observable re-evaluated at runtime (not folded to a static or frozen value).
Ensemble mean of U(T) matches the independent exact pure-death CTMC law within the DKW/4-sigma control and is separated from the frozen-observable wrong law.
Pinned BNG2 source-lowering fact (_rateLaw1() = k_gather*U() on the generated map rule) is reproduced by the pinned BNG2 revision above.
Independently built native NFsim agrees distributionally with the NFnext ensemble under the fixed seed set, or is reported NOT_TESTED if unavailable.
notes: The analytic check passed locally for the declared supported shape. This is not a full-release pass: the pinned-native NFsim comparison has not been executed locally and unsupported shapes still fail closed.
